jobs.description:
Looking for a long-term career as a Paralegal? Or currently working as a Legal PA or Legal Secretary and ready for something more hands-on?

This could be an excellent opportunity to take that next step.

We're working with a leading international law firm in Hong Kong looking for someone to join its established Debt Capital Markets team.

You don't necessarily need previous DCM experience. What's important is your attention to detail, strong Mandarin and English language skills, and genuine interest in building a career as a specialist Paralegal.

What's On Offer?

- The opportunity to build a long-term career as a Paralegal
- Hands-on involvement in major domestic and cross-border debt transactions
- Training and support from experienced lawyers
- A competitive package and an internationally recognised firm

What You'll Be Doing

- Assisting with due diligence and reviewing Chinese-language documents
- Preparing and reviewing transaction and disclosure documentation
- Conducting legal and commercial research
- Supporting lawyers throughout live DCM transactions

Who We're Looking For
We're open to candidates currently working as Paralegals, Legal PAs or Legal Secretaries who want to develop their careers in a more transaction-focused role.

You'll need fluent Mandarin and English, excellent organisational skills and the confidence to work with detailed documentation in a busy legal environment.

Importantly, this opportunity is aimed at someone who wants to grow and progress as a Paralegal, rather than using the role simply as a stepping stone towards qualification.

Interested? Apply now or contact Walker Lovell for a confidential conversation.

Main purpose of the role:

To support the IP team on Hong Kong and China trade mark matters, and assist with international trade mark portfolio management

Main duties and responsibilities:

- Prepare and file documents for Hong Kong trade mark applications, registrations and related proceedings
- Maintain trade mark portfolios, including docketing, record updates and deadline monitoring
- Liaise with clients, overseas associates and trade mark offices
- Draft reports on office actions and assist with responses and submissions
- Conduct trade mark clearance searches and prepare search reports
- Conduct trade mark, company and online research
- Support trade mark prosecution, portfolio management and related projects across multiple jurisdictions
- Assist with investigations into potential trade mark infringements and preparation of cease-and-desist letters
- Prepare fee estimates, portfolio summaries and status reports
- Undertake other duties as assigned by fee earners

Person Specifications:

Education / Qualifications / Experience:

- Post-secondary education; diploma or degree preferred
- 3 to 4 years of trade mark experience
- Experience handling national trade mark and Madrid Protocol matters
- Exposure to regional or international trade mark portfolio management
- Knowledge of registered designs and patent formalities is an advantage
- Excellent written and spoken English and Cantonese and/or Mandarin

Knowledge and Technical Skills:

- Good understanding of trade mark prosecution and portfolio management
- Familiarity with Hong Kong and regional trade mark practice and WIPO Madrid System procedures
- Strong drafting, research and communication skills
- Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities
- Proficient in Microsoft Office and legal technology platforms; familiarity with AI tools is an advantage
- Strong attention to detail and accuracy

General Skills:

- Ability to work independently and meet deadlines
- Strong organisational and prioritisation skills
- Team-oriented with a collaborative approach
- Strong client-service and interpersonal skills
- Adaptable, reliable and proactive
- Detail-oriented with good judgement and professionalism

jobs.description:
Description

At Ashurst Perkins Coie, we're helping shape the future economy. With a global team of more than 3,500 legal professionals across 52 offices, we partner with leading organisations to solve complex challenges across a diverse range of industries, with a distinct strength in technology, energy & infrastructure, and financial services. Our people work on market-leading matters that drive innovation, growth, and transformation around the world. For Ashurst Perkins Coie, innovation is our tradition.

Department / Role overview

We are currently looking for a paralegal / Legal Manager to join our Corporate Transactions group. The job holder will work closely with partners, counsel and associates in Hong Kong, Beijing and Shanghai to provide transactional support to ensure that our lawyers can focus on clients' needs and deliver quality and efficient service.

Main Responsibilities

- Draft, review and proofread documents.
- Assist with legal due diligence exercises and prepare legal due diligence questionnaires and reports.
- Attend on-site due diligence trips and meetings.
- Conduct legal and company research and analysis.
- Handle legal translations.
- Assist with verification of disclosure documents.
- Assist with the signing and completion of the transactions.

Risk and Control: Ensure that all activities and duties are carried out in full compliance with our regulatory requirements and internal policies.

Essential Skills And Experience

- A university law degree/ Master of Law with excellent academic achievements.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English and native Mandarin speaker;
- Willingness to travel frequently for due diligence trips and printer sessions;
- Ability to demonstrate initiative, maturity and common sense with good judgment;
- Good work ethic and ability to work to deadlines.
- Good organisational skills and attention to detail.
- Ideally with relevant 1-2 years' experience in IPO and M&A.

Background checks

In order to comply with regulatory and client requirements, the Firm will undertake appropriate vetting of staff. When applicants accept a job offer, the Firm, alongside a specialist provider, will undertake professional verification and background checks. These checks are only undertaken with consent, and in accordance with our legal and regulatory obligations.

jobs.description:
Company Description

Hong Kong - Shenzhen - Guangzhou - Shanghai - Beijing

JPC Texson Ltd, established since 1990, is a Hong Kong and China licensed Employment Consulting firm, specializes in Headhunting and Recruiting Services for companies in Hong Kong and China. We have offices in Hong Kong, Shenzhen, Guangzhou, Shanghai and Beijing.

Company Overview

- We are a well-established Hong Kong legal firm with over 30 years of history, providing trusted legal services to a wide range of clients.
- Our Conveyancing team comprises around 30 members, and we handle both project conveyancing work for property developers and conveyancing matters for private and corporate clients.
- We offer a professional yet supportive working environment where team members can develop their expertise and build a long-term career.

Role Mission

- To provide efficient and accurate support to the Conveyancing team in handling a diverse portfolio of property transactions, ensuring smooth workflow, timely completion of matters, and excellent client service.

Role Summary

- The Conveyancing Clerk / Conveyancing Paralegal will work as part of a sizeable and experienced Conveyancing team of 30 members.
- This role involves handling both project conveyancing work for property developers and conveyancing matters for private and corporate clients, making it an excellent opportunity for a candidate with solid conveyancing experience and strong file management skills.

Job Description

Job Description

- Handle all aspects of conveyancing matters, including preparation and follow-up of documents.
- Assist with project conveyancing work for property developers as well as conveyancing matters for private and corporate clients.
- Support sales and purchase transactions, mortgage-related matters, and post-completion work.
- Liaise with clients, solicitors, banks, developers, government departments, and other relevant parties.
- Conduct searches, stamping, registration, and related conveyancing procedures.
- Maintain proper filing, record keeping, and case status updates.
- Support the Conveyancing team with ad hoc tasks as required.
- Ensure all matters are handled accurately, efficiently, and within deadlines.

Ideal Candidate

- Over 5 years of solid conveyancing experience.
- Able to handle conveyancing files independently with minimal supervision.
- Good command of English, Chinese & Cantonese; Mandarin is a plus
- Strong sense of responsibility, accuracy, and confidentiality.
- Good interpersonal and communication skills.
- Team player with a proactive and professional working attitude.

Why Join Us

- Join a reputable Hong Kong legal firm with over 30 years of history.
- Be part of a stable and well-structured Conveyancing team of 30 members.
- Gain exposure to both property developer projects and private and corporate client conveyancing matters.
- Enjoy a 5-day work week and a healthy work-life balance.
- Work in a supportive and friendly work culture.
- Build your career in a professional environment with long-term growth potential.

TO APPLY For This Job Or Similar Jobs

Please email your CV with salary expected to resume@jpc.hk

JPC Recruiting Services was established in 1990 and is a Hong Kong–based recruitment firm providing general recruitment and executive search services.

jobs.description:
Mayer Brown is an international law firm positioned to represent the world’s major corporations, funds, and financial institutions in their most important and complex transactions and disputes. We are recognized by our clients as strategic partners with deep commercial instincts and a commitment to creatively anticipating their needs and delivering excellence in everything we do.

We are a collegial, collaborative and diverse firm where highly motivated individuals with an unwavering commitment to excellence receive the opportunity, support and development they need to grow, thrive and realise their greatest potential all while supporting the Firm’s client service principles of excellence, strategic partnership, commercial instinct, integrated strengths, innovation, and collaboration across our international firm.

If you are looking to build your career in a dynamic and supportive environment, and share our commitment to exceptional client service, professionalism, initiative, responsiveness and adaptability, we invite you to join our Hong Kong office.

Responsibilities

We are looking for a highly motivated individual with an unwavering commitment to excellence. The team is busy and is looking for a candidate that has the ability to watch and learn, independently progress their skillset and learning and is able to effectively balance complex, high-stakes work and disruptive hours whilst delivering a high quality work product in a timely manner.

This is an excellent opportunity for a self-motivated and driven individual to work in a premier legal team and become well-versed in a large variety of debt capital markets with wide geographical exposure.

- Provide support to Partners and Associates in Hong Kong.
- Matter management (e.g.: reviewing initial and subsequent drafts and summarizing changes and highlighting changes relevant to the client), handling documentation relating to closings and completion and document checklist review and annotation.

Qualifications

Qualifications, Experience and Personal Attributes

- Paralegal experience from leading U.S. or magic circle legal firms with 3 to 5 years of experience in the Debt Capital Markets practice.
- Fluent in oral and written English.
- The candidate will also need to be comfortable participating in conversations and written communications in Chinese (Mandarin and Cantonese) and able to review drafts in Chinese.

Experience And Attributes

- This is a permanent paralegal position in Mayer Brown’s Corporate & Securities practice.
- Our clients are leading global banks and we are looking for a candidate that can perform routine tasks independently and to a high service quality that is expected from our clients.
- The practice is high volume and day-to-day work will require a thorough understanding of documentation and timelines. The candidate will need excellent organizational skills and demonstrate the ability to manage multiple projects each with a different scope of work in an efficient, high quality and timely manner.
- The debt capital markets practice often requires coverage outside of regular working hours and the candidate will be responsible for attending to and handling tasks during non-work hours and on weekends.

Team Overview

The Hong Kong Legal Team provides practical, business-focused legal support that enables sustainable growth, manages regulatory risk, and protects the company's interests across Hong Kong and the broader APAC region. The team currently comprises two senior lawyers, including one lawyer supporting both Hong Kong and the Philippines, with additional operational support from a Legal Operations Associate based in the Philippines. Reporting to the Hong Kong Legal Team, this role offers the opportunity to work closely with senior legal professionals and cross-functional stakeholders, gaining broad exposure to commercial, corporate, compliance, and operational legal matters in a dynamic international environment. This is a hybrid position and involves regular performance of job responsibilities virtually as well as in-person at an assigned TU office location for a minimum of two days a week.

Role Overview And Core Responsibilities

Role Purpose

The Legal Executive / Paralegal supports the efficient delivery of legal services by managing legal operations, coordinating commercial contracting activities, supporting corporate governance and compliance initiatives, and maintaining effective legal processes. This role helps reduce legal and operational risk, improve business efficiency, and enable internal stakeholders to make informed business decisions while ensuring compliance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements.

Key Responsibilities

- Support the review, preparation, execution, and administration of commercial agreements, including non-disclosure agreements (NDAs), vendor agreements, customer contracts, and related legal documentation to facilitate business operations and growth.
- Manage contract lifecycle activities, including document filing, version control, execution tracking, records management, and reporting to improve operational efficiency and legal oversight.
- Conduct legal and regulatory research and prepare summaries, memos, and supporting materials to assist legal counsel in providing timely advice to business stakeholders.
- Coordinate corporate governance and company secretarial matters, including maintaining statutory records, preparing corporate documentation, and supporting regulatory filings where required.
- Assist with data privacy, compliance, and regulatory initiatives by organizing documentation, monitoring obligations, and supporting implementation of legal and policy requirements.
- Review external-facing communications, marketing materials, and other business content to help ensure alignment with legal, regulatory, and brand requirements.
- Maintain and update legal templates, knowledge resources, trackers, policies, and standard procedures to support consistency, efficiency, and risk management across the organization.
- Coordinate with internal stakeholders, including business, product, compliance, finance, human resources, and regional legal teams, to facilitate efficient legal operations and timely resolution of legal matters.
- Support the management of external counsel, legal vendors, invoices, and administrative processes to ensure effective utilization of legal resources and budget management.
- Assist with special projects, strategic initiatives, and other legal matters as assigned by the legal team.

Required Knowledge And Experiences

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Law, Legal Studies, or a related discipline.
- Minimum 1-3 years of relevant experience as a Legal Executive, Paralegal, Legal Assistant, or similar legal support professional.
- Demonstrated experience supporting commercial contracting and legal document management in either an in-house legal department or law firm environment.
- Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, maintain accuracy, and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environm…

jobs.description:
The firm

Simpson Thacher is seeking a career paralegal to join our Hong Kong office or Tokyo office. The Paralegal is responsible for performing a broad variety of work during all phases of various transactions within their specific practice area. This role works under the supervision and direction of an experienced attorney.

Description/Job Summary

- Assist attorneys with preparation of legal documents, due diligence review, subscription document review and tracking, and related tasks
- Translation of documents
- Complete forms required for the formation/dissolution/amendment and qualification of corporations, LLC’s and partnerships
- Organize and maintain electronic files, and paper files where necessary
- Organize and maintain due diligence and subscription documents
- Perform due diligence searches
- Utilize and manage electronic databases
- Proofread, organize and track documents; prepare closing sets of necessary documents following completion of a transaction; organize and distribute post-closing documents
- Assist with document/information gathering, logistics and coordination of items received
- Maintain well organized files
- Update document management platforms and databases and categorize documents for efficient accessibility
- Liaise with internal departments and outside vendors
- Perform other tasks as assigned by deal teams
- Be flexible to adjust hours to meet departmental need

Required Skills

- Fluency in both English and Chinese or additional languages such as Korean or Japanese
- Detail oriented, with excellent organizational and communication skills
- Able to work in a fast paced environment, both independently or on a team
- Flexibility, time management and an ability to prioritize tasks and deadlines
- Proficiency with legal terminology relevant to the industry
- Critical thinking and solution oriented mindset
- Present information clearly and concisely, both verbally and in writing
- Self-starter who can organize, plan and complete multi-task work activities
- Ability to proofread for contextual, grammatical and spelling errors

Preferred Skills

- Related experience in a law firm or other professional services firm
- Knowledge of MS Office applications and Excel preferred

Required Education

Bachelor’s degree or Law degree required

jobs.description:
Withers

Job title: Paralegal (Family)

Location: Hong Kong

About Withers

A law firm focused on people, performance, and collaboration.

For the past 130 years, we have supported some of the world’s most remarkable people and organizations at defining moments in their lives.

We are united in our commitment to integrity, quality and collaboration. We have a culture of high performance and deliver excellent service consistently across the firm. We provide tailored solutions built on trust and partner with our clients to achieve their goals.

Many of our clients are shaping the future and creating solutions to tackle many of the world’s problems. It makes for a fascinating and challenging practice.

Our role is to get to know each individual client, find out where they want to be, and help them to get there – whether they are building a business, buying a home or protecting and defending their interests.

To meet their unique needs we are exceptionally collaborative, working together across teams and time zones. And we are agile – focusing on strategy rather than rigid ideas and traditional hierarchy.

Join us to be part of a team that is always looking to the future. Where initiative, big ideas and bold moves are always encouraged. Where you can truly be yourself.

What are we looking for?

We are looking to recruit an experienced paralegal to join the Withers Hong Kong's Family team. The role will at times be fast paced so you will need to be an efficient worker who can prioritise tasks and have great organisational skills.

The ideal candidate will be technically capable, have a good working attitude and possess excellent communication skills. This position requires someone who is comfortable using their initiative, is a strong team player and is motivated to produce quality support to the Division.

Areas Of Focus And Responsibilities

- Preparing and drafting pleadings, affidavits, documents and correspondences
- Performing legal research
- Compiling bundles for court hearings
- Simple translation tasks

This list of duties and responsibilities is not exhaustive. It is intended to describe the general content of, and requirements for the performance of this job, and as such, the role may also include the undertaking of additional tasks as required.

Technical Skills And Qualifications

- Candidates with prior experience in a law firm will be preferred
- Able to comply with deadlines and meticulous
- Proficient in PC skills (e.g. Word, Excel & etc.)

Information for Recruitment Agencies

Withers endeavours to recruit and fill vacancies directly. However, when we do need to engage with agencies, Withers operates a preferred supplier list and will not be accepting unsolicited applications from non-PSL agencies for this role.

Equal Opportunities Employment Statement

It is the policy of Withers to provide equal opportunities for all employees in relation to recruitment, training and promotion. Decisions in these areas will be made only by reference to the requirements of the job and shall not be influenced by any consideration of ethnic origin, religion, sex, age, sexual orientation or disability.

Apply Now

jobs.description:
Jones Day is a global law firm with 40 offices in major centers of business and finance throughout the world. Covering 19 countries on five continents, our unique governance system fosters an unparalleled level of integration and contributes to our ranking as one of the best in the world in client service.

Jones Day seeks to employ the most qualified people, capable of delivering superior client service through professional excellence and teamwork, for every position in the Firm. We offer competitive compensation and benefits in a stimulating work environment.

Are you interested in the opportunity to work for a global leading law firm that will give you the experience and exposure you need to build your knowledge and skills as well as advance your career? If you are, then Jones Day may be the firm for you.

Summary of Essential Duties and Responsibilities:
Paralegals attend due diligence interviews; perform precedent and other ad-hoc legal research; conduct prospectus verification and other IPO-related tasks; assist in preparation of various documents (e.g. A1 documents, prospectuses, due diligence questionnaires etc.); prepare English-Chinese translation of legal documents; and organise client meetings and taking minutes.

Required Qualifications:

- Law degree is an advantage but not a must.
- Preferably with prior work experience in capital markets.
- Excellent command of written and verbal English and Mandarin.
- Strong communication skills and great attention to detail.
- Ability to work independently and in a fast-paced and driven environment.
- Sound knowledge in the use of computer and various IT programs.
- Occasional travel to PRC may be required.
- Immediate availability preferred.

ONLY RESUMES (C.V.s) IN .PDF FORMAT WILL BE ACCEPTED AND REVIEWED
*Principals only – No search firms.

jobs.description:
Introduction: We are partnering with a top-tier international law firm to hire a Debt Capital Markets Paralegal for their growing Corporate & Securities practice in Hong Kong. The position provides direct exposure to market-leading DCM transactions across the APAC region, working alongside highly regarded Partners.

Responsibilities:

- Supporting Partners and Senior Associates on high-volume, cross-border Debt Capital Markets transactions.
- Assisting with matter management, including reviewing initial and subsequent draft documentation, summarizing key revisions, and highlighting critical changes for clients.
- Managing closing and completion documentation, checklist reviews, and detailed annotations.
- Executing routine legal tasks independently while maintaining high service delivery standards for global banking clients.
- Coordinating transaction timelines and managing multiple concurrent projects efficiently under tight schedules.
- Overseeing deal logistics and providing coverage outside standard working hours when required by transaction flows.
Requirements:

- Possess 3 to 5 years of solid DCM paralegal experience gained from leading US or Magic Circle law firms.
- Strong background in Debt Capital Markets is preferred, though candidates with broader Corporate Finance experience covering a high proportion of DCM will be considered.
- Professional fluency in written and spoken English, Cantonese, and Mandarin, including the ability to review Chinese draft legal documents.
- Exceptional organizational skills with a proven track record of handling high-stakes, time-sensitive transactional work.
- Ability to work independently, demonstrate strong learning agility, and manage demanding client expectations effectively.
For a more comprehensive list of current opportunities, please visit www.ambition.com.hk

jobs.description:
Practice Group / Department:

Business Partnering - Hong Kong

Job Description

We're Norton Rose Fulbright - a global law firm with over 50 offices and 7,000 employees worldwide. We provide the world’s preeminent corporations and financial institutions with a full business law service.

As well as the relevant skills and experience, we're looking for people who are innovative, commercial and value the work that they do. We celebrate multiple approaches and points of view and believe diversity drives innovation, so we're building a culture where difference is valued.

Take the first step towards a career at Norton Rose Fulbright

Norton Rose Fulbright Hong Kong is part of Norton Rose Fulbright, a global legal practice providing the world's pre-eminent corporations and financial institutions with a full business law service from offices across Europe, the United States, Canada, Latin America, Asia, Australia, Africa and the Middle East.

We currently have an opening for Trainee Solicitor (2029) position in our Hong Kong office.

We look for applications from candidates with law degree, who demonstrate a consistently strong academic record. You are expected to have or be expecting at least an upper second class degree or equivalent. We look for people who are team players, with excellent interpersonal and communication skills.

Requirement

- Strong academic record: at least 2:1 degree or equivalent
- Good communication skills
- Commercial awareness
- Negotiation skills
- Team playrer
- Leadership qualities
- Fluency in English (both written and spoken)
- Knowledge of Chinese (both written and spoken)

Please ensure you include your resume, cover letter indicating the year you intend to commence a training contract in Hong Kong, and the final/latest transcripts of your high schoold and university in your application.

You can upload all supporting documents, including your resume, cover letter, and academic transcripts from both high school and university, to the Resume/Cover Letter Upload section.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

To attract the best people, we strive to create a diverse and inclusive environment where everyone can bring their whole selves to work, have a sense of belonging, and realize their full career potential.

Our new enabled work model allows our people to have more flexibility in the way they choose to work from both the office and a remote location, while continuing to deliver the highest standards of service. We offer a range of family friendly and inclusive employment policies and provide access to programmes and services aimed at nurturing our people’s health and overall wellbeing. Find more about Diversity, Equity and Inclusion here.

We are proud to be an equal opportunities employer and encourage applications from individuals who can complement our existing teams. We strive to create an inclusive and accessible recruitment process for all candidates. If you require any tailored adjustments or accommodations, please let us know via EMEARecruitment@nortonrosefulbright.com
